rationale:
The subject has one obligation. `node_id` must borrow the identity of the source node being checked, and the signature returns `&NodeId<D>`.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[labeled_selections_track_only_target_membership_without_reading_contents]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds `ValidationContext::new(&graph, intern_node(1))` and asserts `ctx.node_id() == &intern_node(1)`. That checks the returned value is the node the context was created for, and the `&` comparison shows it is a borrow.

The same test then queries a different node (9) and a different label. This shows the source identity is separate from the nodes queried. The test also uses a second context for node 1 in later steps.

The borrowed return type is enforced by compilation. The public API test, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, covers export listing only.

I found no plausible violating behavior the assertions would accept. The one assertion is made before any query, and the other node ids it could be confused with (9 and the successors) differ from 1.

text: Borrow the identity of the source node being checked.
